title: The role of ETFS amino acids on the stability and inhibition of p53-MDM2 complex of anticancer p53-derivatives peptides: Density functional theory and molecular docking studies.
authors: Soriano-Correa, Catalina; Vichi-Ramirez, Micheel Merari; Herrera-Valencia, Edtson E; Barrientos-Salcedo, Carolina
one_liner_zh: 该文用DFT和分子对接研究抗癌p53衍生肽与MDM2的相互作用，虽涉及蛋白-肽结合建模，但对象为p53-MDM2蛋白-蛋白体系而非蛋白质-DNA互作，方法可迁移性有限。
abstract: Cancer is one of the leading causes of mortality in the world. Despite the existence of diverse antineoplastic treatments, these do not possess the expected efficacy in many cases. Knowledge of the molecular mechanisms involved in tumor processes allows the identification of a greater number of therapeutic targets employed in the study of new anticancer drugs. In the last decades, peptide-based therapy design using computational chemistry has gained importance in the field of oncology therapeutics. This work aims to evaluate the electronic structure, physicochemical properties, stability, and inhibition of ETFS amino acids and peptides derived from the p53-MDM2 binding domain with action in cancer cells; by means of chemical descriptors at the DFT-BHandHLYP level in an aqueous solution, and its intermolecular interactions through molecular docking studies. The results show that The ETFS fragment plays a critical role in the intermolecular interactions. Thus, the amino acids E17, T18 and S20 increase intermolecular interactions through hydrogen bonds and enhance structural stability. F19, W23 and V25 enhance the formation of the alpha-helix. The hydrogen bonds formed by the backbone atoms for PNC-27, PNC-27-B and PNC-28 stabilize the alpha-helices more than hydrogen bonds formed by the side chains atoms. Also, molecular docking indicated that the PNC27B-MDM2, PNC28B-MDM2, PNC27-MDM2 and PNC28A-MDM2 complexes show the best binding energy. Therefore, DFT and molecular docking studies showed that the proposed peptides: PNC-28B, PNC-27B and PNC-28A could inhibit the binding of MDM2 to the p53 protein, decreasing the translocation and degradation of p53 native protein.
abstract_zh: 癌症是全球主要死亡原因之一。尽管存在多种抗肿瘤治疗方法，但在许多情况下这些方法并未展现出预期的疗效。对肿瘤过程中涉及的分子机制的了解，有助于识别更多用于研究新型抗癌药物的治疗靶点。近几十年来，利用计算化学进行基于肽的治疗设计在肿瘤治疗领域日益重要。本研究旨在评估源自p53-MDM2结合域的ETFS氨基酸及其衍生肽在癌细胞作用中的电子结构、理化性质、稳定性和抑制作用；通过在水溶液中的DFT-BHandHLYP水平化学描述符，以及通过分子对接研究其分子间相互作用。结果表明，ETFS片段在分子间相互作用中起关键作用。因此，氨基酸E17、T18和S20通过氢键增强分子间相互作用并提高结构稳定性。F19、W23和V25增强α-螺旋的形成。对于PNC-27、PNC-27-B和PNC-28，主链原子形成的氢键比侧链原子形成的氢键更能稳定α-螺旋。此外，分子对接表明PNC27B-MDM2、PNC28B-MDM2、PNC27-MDM2和PNC28A-MDM2复合物显示出最佳结合能。因此，DFT和分子对接研究表明，所提出的肽：PNC-28B、PNC-27B和PNC-28A可能抑制MDM2与p53蛋白的结合，减少天然p53蛋白的转位和降解。
